newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks post 16th record close of 1997.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks post 16th record close of 1997.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks posted their 16th record close of 1997 on Friday * TSE buoyed by strong gold shares and a rally in New York * 92 million shares traded worth C$1.4 billion.
Toronto stocks inched above previous records to post another closing high on Friday, aided by a rocketing New York market and stronger gold sector.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 42.62 points to 6492.10, just a shade above the previous peak for the year. It also set a new all-time high of 6498.52 points late in the day.
"It's just a matter of a significant amount of money chasing few prospects," said RBC Dominion Securities Investment Advisor Ira Katzin.
About 92 million shares were traded worth C$1.43 billion.

In New York, the Dow Jones Industrial Average lept 130 points as investors cheered a mixed bag of May U.S. employment data, convinced that it showed the economy was growing without any inflation, analysts said.
Canada's bond market also rallied. The 30-year benchmark bond closed C$1.94 higher at C$114.32 to yield 6.867 percent.
Twelve of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes ended stronger, led by conglomerates, golds, consumer products and transportation.
There were modest losses in forestry products and real estate . Advancing issues soared past declines 586 to 359.
Another 311 stocks were unchanged.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* Merger mania dominated the oil patch on Friday. CS Resources Ltd jumped 3.70 to 15.00 in active trading after Gulf Canada Resources Ltd said it planned to offer C$413 million for CS Resources. Gulf shares fell 0.45 to 11.90.

* Gandalf Technologies Inc lost 0.97 to close at 1.63 in heavy trading. The computer network equipment maker said late on Thursday it was almost out of money and mulling several offers for its undervalued business.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8109))
